_what: M11a T3: why model_fp16.onnx is NOT published. CPU parity qualifies an fp16 graph only because CPUExecutionProvider up-converts it to fp32 -- which is also why it is ~8x SLOWER there. On CUDA, where it actually runs in fp16, it disagrees with the fp32 reference on 255 of 259 real passages. A CPU-only parity gate cannot see this.
decision: fp32 only. model_fp16.onnx is not in the released manifest. The converter + repair path is retained in m11/release/export_doc.py behind --fp16 as an experimental build, not a shipped artifact.
fixtures: m11/release/doc_fixtures.json, 259 real nq-250k passages, six length strata

environment.onnxruntime_gpu: 1.20.2 (throwaway venv; the release venv keeps CPU-only onnxruntime 1.29.0)
environment.note: the release venv was NOT modified -- swapping onnxruntime for onnxruntime-gpu would disturb the live `zero` gates

cuda_fp32_vs_cpu_fp32.verdict: the fp32 artifact is correct on CUDA. No TF32 degradation, so the published graph needs no accelerator caveat.

cuda_fp16_vs_cpu_fp32.verdict: unusable for retrieval. Not a long-input effect -- every stratum is hit, from 7 tokens up.

cpu_fp16_vs_torch_fp32.verdict: PASSES mandate 11.4, and is MISLEADING. ORT has no fast CPU fp16 kernels, so it up-converts; this number certifies fp32 arithmetic on fp16 weights.

cuda_latency.verdict: the speedup is real and irrelevant -- it buys 1.78x on outputs that are wrong.

transferable_lesson: A CPU parity gate does not qualify a reduced-precision ONNX graph. Measure on the execution provider the precision exists for, or do not ship the precision.
what_would_change_it: An fp16 export whose CUDA output matches the fp32 reference on the full fixture set -- e.g. keeping attention/softmax accumulation in fp32 via a wider node_block_list, or an fp16 export produced by a path that controls accumulation dtype rather than a post-hoc graph cast.
